lead: Lexington plumbing deals with hard limestone water, karst ground, cold snaps and older homes near downtown. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across Lexington.
risk: hard water scale, aging pipes in older homes and frozen pipes
risk_short: hard water, old pipes and frozen pipes
why: Chevy Chase, Ashland Park and the University area have homes from the 1910s to the 1950s with galvanized supply lines and cast-iron or clay drains.
Lexington sits on limestone with sinkholes in places, which can shift buried lines. Winter cold snaps freeze pipes in crawl spaces and exterior walls.
water: Kentucky American Water treats water from the Kentucky River and Jacobson Reservoir. Water from limestone country is hard, so scale builds up in heaters and on fixtures.
tips: Scope the sewer line before buying an older home.
areas: PipeMend works in Chevy Chase, Ashland Park, the University area, Hamburg, Beaumont, Downtown, Kenwick and every other Lexington neighborhood.
permits: Kentucky's Division of Plumbing licenses plumbers and oversees plumbing permits and inspections across the state, including Lexington.

faq.a: Lexington is in limestone country. The water picks up calcium and magnesium from the rock, which leaves scale in water heaters and on fixtures. A softener and yearly flushing help.
